nodes.label: Light direction
aliases: which side the light is on
nodes.description: The branch for where the main light sits in relation to the subject - in front, to one side, behind, above or below - because that is what decides where the shadows fall.
examples: light coming from the left of the subject
the sun behind the person's head
nodes.prompt_fragment: with a clear main light direction

nodes.label: Light quality
nodes.description: The branch for how sharp or gentle the light is: hard light draws shadows with crisp dark edges, soft light lets them fade away gradually.
examples: knife-edged shadow on a wall
shadows that melt away softly
nodes.prompt_fragment: with a distinct quality of light
nodes.negative_fragment: with no particular quality of light

nodes.label: Light source
nodes.description: The branch for what is actually producing the light - daylight, a window, a flash, a street lamp, a candle or a studio head.
examples: a single window lighting a room
a neon sign lighting a face
nodes.prompt_fragment: lit by an identifiable light source

nodes.label: Lighting pattern
nodes.description: The branch for named lighting looks - recognisable recipes such as high key, low key, silhouette or Rembrandt that photographers reuse by name.
examples: a bright white high-key portrait
a face half swallowed by shadow

nodes.label: Colour temperature
nodes.description: The branch for whether the light looks orange-warm, blue-cool or plain white, which is often the first thing a viewer feels about a picture without noticing why.
examples: orange lamplight in a dark room
cold blue light before sunrise

nodes.label: Front lighting
nodes.description: The main light comes from roughly where the camera is, so the subject is evenly lit and the shadows fall behind them where you cannot see them.
examples: a face lit evenly with no visible shadow side
a passport-style even light

nodes.label: Side lighting
nodes.description: The light arrives from the left or the right, so one side of the subject is bright and the other slides into shadow, which brings out texture and shape.
examples: a face bright on one cheek and dark on the other
raking light across a rough wall

nodes.label: Three-quarter lighting
nodes.description: The light sits about halfway between the camera and the side of the subject, the standard portrait position that shapes a face without hiding half of it.
examples: a portrait lit from front-left at about 45 degrees
gentle shaping on one cheek
nodes.negative_fragment: not lit from a three-quarter angle

nodes.label: Backlighting
nodes.description: The main light is behind the subject and shines back towards the camera, tracing a bright edge around them and often making the background glow.
examples: hair glowing against a low sun
a figure edged in light in a doorway

nodes.label: Rim lighting
aliases: halo of light around the subject
nodes.description: A narrow bright line traces the edge of the subject and lifts them off a darker background; it usually comes from a light placed behind and slightly to one side, and it sits happily on top of any other lighting.
examples: a bright outline along a shoulder and jaw
glowing edge on hair against a dark street
nodes.prompt_fragment: with a bright rim light along the edges
nodes.negative_fragment: with no rim light on the edges

nodes.label: Top lighting
nodes.description: The light comes from directly above, dropping shadows into the eye sockets and under the nose and chin - the look of midday sun or a bare ceiling lamp.
examples: dark eye sockets under a noon sun
a pool of light straight down onto a table

nodes.label: Under lighting
nodes.description: The light comes from below the face, which reverses the shadows we expect to see and makes almost any subject look uncanny or theatrical.
examples: a face lit by a campfire from below
a torch held under the chin

nodes.label: Hard light
nodes.description: The light comes from a small or very distant source, so shadows have crisp edges and the jump between lit and unlit areas is abrupt.
examples: a sharp-edged shadow of a railing on a wall
bright highlights next to black shadow
nodes.prompt_fragment: hard directional light with crisp shadows

nodes.label: Soft light
nodes.description: The light comes from a large or scattered source, so shadows fade out gradually and skin, fabric and faces look gentle rather than carved.
examples: a portrait with shadows that fade away slowly
light wrapping around a cheek
nodes.prompt_fragment: soft light with gentle shadow edges

nodes.label: Flat lighting
nodes.description: There is almost no visible shadow anywhere, so the subject looks evenly lit and slightly two-dimensional - what you get from a grey sky or a flash fired straight at someone.
examples: an evenly lit face with no shadow side
a grey overcast street with no shadows

nodes.label: Diffused light
nodes.description: The light has been scattered on its way to the subject - by cloud, a curtain, a softbox or a sheet of fabric - so it arrives from many directions at once and barely casts a shadow.
examples: daylight through a thin white curtain
light through a scrim on set

nodes.label: Natural light
nodes.description: The scene is lit by the sun or the sky rather than by lamps, whether that means bright sun, open shade or daylight coming through a window.
examples: a room lit only by the windows
a street lit by afternoon sun

nodes.label: Artificial light
nodes.description: The scene is lit by man-made lights - studio heads, flash, street lamps, neon signs or whatever lamps happen to be in the room.
examples: an office lit by ceiling tubes
a portrait lit by studio strobes

nodes.label: Window light
nodes.description: Daylight comes in through a window and reaches the subject mostly from one side, giving a soft light that falls off quickly across the room - a favourite for indoor portraits.
examples: a person sitting beside a bright window
soft daylight across a kitchen table
nodes.prompt_fragment: soft daylight coming through a window

nodes.label: Golden hour sunlight
nodes.description: The sun sits low just after sunrise or before sunset, so the light is warm and orange, arrives almost horizontally and throws long soft shadows.
examples: long shadows across a field at sunset
warm light raking down a street

nodes.label: Harsh midday sun
nodes.description: The sun is high and unobstructed, giving very bright highlights, deep hard-edged shadows and subjects who squint.
examples: black shadows under a midday sun
a bleached white wall at noon

nodes.label: Overcast daylight
nodes.description: A blanket of cloud turns the whole sky into one enormous soft light, so shadows are faint, contrast is low and colours look slightly cool.
examples: a grey-sky portrait with almost no shadows
a beach on a cloudy afternoon

nodes.label: Open shade
nodes.description: The subject stands out of the direct sun but still under open sky, so the light is soft, even and usually a little blue.
examples: a portrait in the shadow of a building
someone under a tree on a sunny day

nodes.label: Moonlight
nodes.description: A dim, cool, bluish night light with the sky as its only source, so only the brightest parts of the scene keep any detail.
examples: a pale blue field under a full moon
moonlight through a bedroom window

nodes.label: Direct flash
nodes.description: A bare flash fires straight at the subject, giving bright punchy light, hard shadows and the deliberately raw snapshot look used in party and fashion photography.
examples: a night street portrait with a bright flash
harsh flash on a face at a party

nodes.label: On-camera flash
nodes.description: The flash sits right at the lens, so the light is dead frontal, the subject looks flat and bright, and a hard shadow is stamped on the wall right behind them.
examples: a flat bright face with a shadow outline on the wall
a snapshot lit by a camera's own flash

nodes.label: Bounce flash
nodes.description: The flash is aimed at a ceiling or wall instead of the subject, so a big patch of that surface becomes the real light source and the result looks soft and natural.
examples: an indoor event photo with soft even light
flash bounced off a white ceiling

nodes.label: Streetlight
nodes.description: The subject is lit by public lighting at night, usually a warm orange or greenish pool of light with darkness between the lamps.
examples: a figure under an orange street lamp
wet asphalt lit by city lamps
nodes.prompt_fragment: lit by orange streetlight at night

nodes.label: Neon light
nodes.description: Coloured signs and tubes throw saturated pink, blue or green light onto the subject - the signature look of night streets and cyberpunk imagery.
examples: a face washed in pink and cyan neon
a bar sign reflected on wet pavement

nodes.label: Practical lights
nodes.description: The lights doing the work are visible inside the frame - table lamps, bare bulbs, screens or signs - which makes the lighting feel like it belongs to the place.
examples: a room lit by two visible table lamps
a face lit by a laptop screen
nodes.prompt_fragment: lit by practical lamps visible in the frame

nodes.label: Candlelight
nodes.description: A small flame lights the subject from close range, so the light is very warm, falls away quickly and leaves most of the scene in darkness.
examples: a face over a birthday cake
a dinner table lit by two candles

nodes.label: Firelight
nodes.description: A fire lights the scene from below or to one side with an unsteady orange glow that moves and flickers.
examples: faces around a campfire
a fireplace lighting a dark room

nodes.label: Studio softbox
nodes.description: A large fabric box in front of a studio light turns it into a broad soft source - the everyday workhorse of controlled portrait and product lighting.
examples: a clean studio portrait on grey
a product lit by one large soft box

nodes.label: Beauty dish
nodes.description: A shallow metal dish placed above and in front of the face gives light that is crisp but still flattering, with a fast shadow fall-off - the classic beauty and cosmetics look.
examples: a cosmetics portrait with sculpted cheekbones
a crisp studio headshot

nodes.label: Ring light
nodes.description: A circle of light around the lens lights the face perfectly frontally, leaving an even wash, a thin shadow outline behind the subject and a doughnut-shaped reflection in the eyes.
examples: a streamer's evenly lit face
a beauty shot with ring catchlights in the eyes

nodes.label: Spotlight
nodes.description: A narrow focused beam lights only part of the scene, leaving a bright pool with everything around it dropping into darkness.
examples: a singer in a pool of light on a dark stage
one lit chair in an empty room
nodes.prompt_fragment: a hard spotlight picking the subject out of darkness

nodes.label: High key
nodes.description: Nearly everything in the picture is bright with very few dark tones, giving a clean, light, often cheerful look.
examples: a portrait on a white background with almost no shadows
a bright airy interior shot
nodes.prompt_fragment: high-key lighting with bright, airy tones

nodes.label: Low key
nodes.description: Most of the frame sits in shadow and only small parts are lit, producing a dark, dramatic and often mysterious mood.
examples: a face emerging from a black background
a dark bar interior with one lit table

nodes.label: Chiaroscuro
nodes.description: A painterly extreme of light against dark, borrowed from old-master painting: one strong light carves the subject out of near-black surroundings.
examples: a lit hand and face against total darkness
an old-master style portrait
nodes.prompt_fragment: chiaroscuro lighting, the subject carved out of deep darkness

nodes.label: Silhouette
aliases: black shape against a bright background
nodes.description: The subject is left completely dark against a much brighter background, so only their outline reads and no detail of face or clothing survives.
examples: a black figure in a bright doorway
two people cut out against a sunset

nodes.label: Backlit haze
nodes.description: Light shining towards the camera catches dust, mist or smoke in the air, so the picture glows, contrast drops and visible beams may appear.
examples: sunbeams through trees in morning mist
a hazy glow around a backlit figure
nodes.prompt_fragment: hazy backlight glowing through the air

nodes.label: Split lighting
aliases: light on one side of the face
nodes.description: The light comes from exactly the side, so one half of the face is lit and the other half falls into shadow, split down the line of the nose.
examples: a face lit on the left, dark on the right
a dramatic half-shadow headshot
nodes.prompt_fragment: split lighting dividing the face into light and shadow

nodes.label: Rembrandt lighting
aliases: triangle of light on the cheek
nodes.description: A portrait pattern where a light at roughly 45 degrees leaves a small triangle of light on the shadowed cheek, named after the painter who used it.
examples: a small lit triangle under the eye on the shadow side
a moody painterly headshot
nodes.prompt_fragment: Rembrandt lighting with a small triangle of light on the cheek

nodes.label: Butterfly lighting
nodes.description: The light sits directly above and in front of the face, dropping a small butterfly-shaped shadow beneath the nose - the classic glamour portrait pattern.
examples: a symmetric beauty portrait with a small nose shadow
an old Hollywood star portrait
nodes.prompt_fragment: butterfly lighting from directly above the face

nodes.label: Loop lighting
nodes.description: A gentle portrait pattern where the light is a little to one side and slightly above, leaving a small loop of shadow from the nose onto the cheek.
examples: a natural-looking headshot with a soft nose shadow
an everyday flattering portrait light
nodes.prompt_fragment: loop lighting with a small nose shadow

nodes.label: Coloured gel lighting
nodes.description: Coloured sheets are placed over the lights so the subject is lit in deliberate colours - magenta on one side and cyan on the other, for example.
examples: a portrait lit red on one side and blue on the other
a music-video style coloured wash
nodes.negative_fragment: no coloured gels on the lights

nodes.label: Dappled light
nodes.description: The light passes through leaves, blinds or a lattice before it reaches the subject, scattering bright patches and shadow shapes across them.
examples: leaf shadows moving across a face
stripes of blind shadow on a wall
nodes.prompt_fragment: dappled light falling in patches across the subject

nodes.label: Warm light
nodes.description: The light leans orange or golden, which usually reads as warm, cosy or nostalgic.
examples: a living room glowing with lamplight
skin warmed by late sun

nodes.label: Cool light
nodes.description: The light leans blue, which usually reads as cold, clinical, nocturnal or calm.
examples: a blue-grey morning street
a clinical office under white-blue tubes

nodes.label: Neutral colour temperature
nodes.description: The light is close to plain white with no obvious orange or blue cast, so colours look much as they would to the eye.
examples: a clean product shot with true colours
a neutral studio portrait

nodes.label: Mixed colour temperature
nodes.description: Two or more differently coloured lights share the scene - warm lamplight indoors against cool blue daylight through the window, for instance.
examples: orange room light against blue dusk outside
a face half warm, half neon blue
nodes.prompt_fragment: mixed warm and cool light sources
